title: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
question: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
answer: TCP is a connection-oriented, reliable transport protocol: it performs a three-way handshake, acknowledges received segments, retransmits lost data and delivers bytes in order. UDP is connectionless and unreliable -- it sends datagrams with no handshake, acknowledgement or ordering guarantees, which makes it lower-latency and ideal for real-time traffic such as voice, video and DNS. TCP is used where integrity matters (web, email, file transfer); UDP is used where speed matters more than guaranteed delivery.
